research_concepts: teammate DRIVE preceding PNR as a sequential-action context effect
play-type labels derived from NBA stats play-by-play action types and sub-types
derived possession records (initiator, play type, points) in the graph database
same-player versus teammate sequential premiums relative to baseline PPP
methodological_questions: Does any teammate DRIVE immediately preceding a PNR possession raise PNR PPP relative to matched PNRs without it?
How accurate are the PNR and DRIVE labels in the derived records, and what fraction of possessions carry a usable play type?
Is the preceding-action contrast confounded by shot quality, shooter and ball-handler identity, defensive matchups, and foul-ending outcomes?
What per-arm sample is needed to detect a plausible PPP difference, given the sparse per-cell counts seen in earlier work?

historical_evidence.finding: Sequential premium scan over same-player and teammate X->Y pairs. Reported cells include P. George DRIVE->SPOT_UP +0.560 (n=31, t=+2.2), L. Doncic DRIVE->PNR +0.309 (n=53), and D. Bane DRIVE->PNR -0.324 (n=70, t=-2.7). Most cells were recorded as DIRECT, and the mechanism was recorded as E_unclear. Limits recorded: label_or_classification_error and small_sample. The record does not specify whether these cells are same-player or teammate sequences, except the ones labeled as such.

Play-type labeling audit. OTHER possessions ended in fouls 36% of the time, which inflated their PPP. DRIVE was 12pp below the foul benchmark. PNR showed a 22% foul rate. Only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%) mapped to a real play type via initiation_type. Verdict recorded as artifact_found. Validation status: no_validation_recorded.

Season stability of top sequential suppressors across 30 stars and 4 seasons, with min n=20 per cell. Only 2/30 (7%) met the 75% same-top-suppressor stability rule. Some teammate DRIVE->SPOT_UP and DRIVE->PNR cells had large negative premiums (e.g., Giannis->Lillard DRIVE->PNR -0.263, n=31). Recorded mechanism: B_powered_null. Validation status: no_validation_recorded.

Shot-level PNR shares of half-court shots for 2024-25 across 30 teams (about 5,994 to 6,581 half-court shots per team). Shares ranged from about 7.6% to 13.8%. Possession-level PNR calibration of about 17.9 to 19.6% of possessions is noted in later logs, but there is no pass/fail gate. Validation status: no_validation_recorded.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Scanning many same-player and teammate X->Y sequence cells for PPP premiums above baseline.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as E_unclear with label_or_classification_error and small_sample limits. Cells are small (n about 30 to 70), signs are mixed across cells, and the record does not establish that any cell is a real effect.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using initiation_type to map possessions to real play types.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as an artifact. Only 0.7% of possessions mapped to a real play type. Foul endings inflated OTHER PPP by 36%, and DRIVE and PNR foul rates distort their benchmarks.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating sequential-suppressor effects as stable across seasons.
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as rejected by an adequately powered null (B_powered_null). Only 2 of 30 stars were stable under the 75% rule, and the cells had small samples (min n=20).

evidence_establishes: Per-cell sequential PPP premiums in the earlier scan are small, noisy, and sign-unstable, with per-cell counts around 30 to 70 (FAM:SF40, FAM:SF-APPA-058).
The initiation_type labeling path mapped almost no possessions to real play types, so PNR and DRIVE labels from that path cannot support a test (FAM:SF-CHT-025).
Foul endings contaminate PPP by play type, so a naive PPP comparison by preceding action is confounded by foul outcomes (FAM:SF-CHT-025).
Possession-level PNR shares from the earlier calibration vary across teams and are not validated against a gate (FAM:SF-APPM-058).
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether a teammate DRIVE directly before a PNR raises PNR PPP. No record tests this specific contrast.

Whether the graph-database possession records (initiator, play type, points) have acceptable precision or recall for PNR and DRIVE. The labeling audit used the initiation_type path, not the graph records.
The true effect size, its sign, or its variance for the preceding-action contrast.
Whether the 2025-26 playoffs data, partial as of 2026-06-14, are usable.
Whether the cited cells are teammate or same-player sequences, except where the record says so.
own_inferences: The question is a sequential-context test and needs labels for both the preceding teammate action and the PNR. Label error at the level recorded in FAM:SF-CHT-025 would dominate any effect of this size.

Under a plausible PPP difference of about 0.05, with per-possession SD near 1.0, a two-arm comparison needs on the order of 6,000 PNR possessions per arm. This is a rough, self-computed estimate, not from any record. Per-cell counts in the earlier scans are far smaller, so per-player or per-pair cells are underpowered.
Foul endings and free-throw trips should be removed or modeled, since FAM:SF-CHT-025 shows they change PPP by play type.
Shot quality is a likely confounder, because a DRIVE that precedes a PNR may change shot selection on the subsequent PNR.
uncertainties: The graph-database possession records were not inspected, so their label accuracy is unknown.
The full text of FAM:SF40, FAM:SF-APPA-058, and FAM:SF-APPM-058 was truncated in retrieval ([cut]). Only the excerpted results were seen.
The data cutoff is 2026-06-14, so 2025-26 playoffs data are incomplete. Regular-season 2025-26 is complete only from 2026-04-13.
No validation of any label set was recorded (no_validation_recorded in each record).
Whether the earlier scan's DRIVE->PNR cells are teammate or same-player sequences is not fully stated.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records show that the play-type labels were not validated, that foul endings distort PPP, and that the earlier sequential-premium scans were small, noisy, and unstable. Together they shifted the decision from proceed to do_not_proceed until the label-validation gate is passed. Had the records been absent, the question might have been proceeded with directly.

blocking_constraints.text: The initiation_type path maps only 0.7% of possessions to a real play type. The graph-database records have not been audited, so precision and recall for DRIVE and PNR are unknown.
PNR and DRIVE labels and PPP come from the same play-by-play pipeline, and the calibrated PNR share (about 18 to 20%) is itself derived rather than observed.
Earlier per-cell samples are around 30 to 70, far below the roughly 6,000 per arm needed for a 0.05 PPP difference. Pair-level or player-level cells will not reach useful power.
Foul endings (FAM:SF-CHT-025), shot quality, shooter and defender identity, and possession context all confound the preceding-action contrast.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests whether a teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP. FAM:SF40 scanned sequential premiums and found mixed, small-sample cells with unclear mechanism. FAM:SF-APPA-058 found sequential suppressors unstable across seasons, rejected by an adequately powered null. FAM:SF-CHT-025 found labeling artifacts from foul endings and a 0.7% mapping rate. FAM:SF-APPM-058 gave shot-level PNR shares without a validation gate. Together these show related work, but none answers this specific question.

risks.text: Play-type labels from initiation_type map only 0.7% of possessions (FAM:SF-CHT-025). Graph-record accuracy is unvalidated.
Foul-ending possessions inflate OTHER PPP by 36% and show a 22% foul rate for PNR (FAM:SF-CHT-025). Foul-driven PPP may mechanically mimic or mask a sequencing effect.
Earlier per-cell samples (n about 20 to 70) cannot detect a plausible PPP difference (FAM:SF40, FAM:SF-APPA-058).
Scanning many X->Y cells produces spurious top cells (FAM:SF40), and no multiplicity correction was recorded.
Selecting the most extreme preceding-action cells inflates apparent premiums, as the top cells in FAM:SF40 illustrate, and they do not persist across seasons (FAM:SF-APPA-058).
Shot quality, shooter and defender identity, and lineup context confound the preceding-action contrast.
Stability across seasons was 2/30 under the 75% rule (FAM:SF-APPA-058), so effects may vary by season or roster.
Without placebo sequences, any preceding-action effect cannot be separated from labeling or selection artifacts.
PNR share is calibrated from derived labels (FAM:SF-APPM-058), so the calibration itself depends on the labels under test.

design.estimand: Gate-conditional. The planned contrast is the difference in PNR PPP between PNR possessions preceded by a teammate DRIVE and matched PNR possessions without one, with a pre-registered minimum effect of interest. Do not estimate until the label gate is passed.
design.unit: PNR possession, with the preceding possession identified from the same play-by-play sequence.
design.sample: Regular seasons 2022-23 through 2024-25 and 2023-24 playoffs and 2024-25 playoffs, plus 2025-26 regular season only after 2026-04-13. Exclude 2025-26 playoffs until the 2026-06-21 completion date. Pre-register a label-audit subsample before any PPP analysis.
design.power: Approximately 6,000 PNR possessions per arm is needed to detect a 0.05 PPP difference at 80% power, assuming a per-possession SD near 1.0 (own estimate, not from any record). Sub-cell power is inadequate and will not be reported as a finding.
design.controls: Exclude or model foul-ending possessions and free-throw trips. Control for expected points from shot distance and result, shooter and ball-handler identity, defensive matchup minutes, lineup, score margin, and clock. Use matched comparisons or player fixed effects.
design.falsification: Placebo contrasts: teammate SPOT_UP or other non-DRIVE actions preceding PNR, and DRIVE preceding non-PNR actions. A real effect should show no comparable premium in placebo contrasts. Also test whether the preceding-action effect replicates across disjoint seasons.
design.multiplicity: One pre-registered primary contrast. Any secondary cells or player-pair scans are exploratory and corrected with Holm or Benjamini-Hochberg across the full family, and are reported as exploratory only.
design.decision_rule: Gate: manual audit of DRIVE and PNR labels on a pre-registered sample must reach at least 0.9 precision on both (own threshold). Only if the gate passes: report the primary contrast with a 95% CI. Supported if the CI excludes 0 at the pre-registered minimum effect and placebo contrasts show no comparable effect. Rejected if the CI is tight around 0 and power is adequate. Uncertain or artifact otherwise.
design.data_version: Frozen snapshot as of 2026-06-14, with the 2025-26 playoffs excluded because they were partial then. The graph-database possession records and the initiation_type path must be versioned and audited before analysis.

Is the preceding-action effect confounded by shot quality, player quality, and possession outcome labels?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 4 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY
